scope: Independent read-only code/test/source review; no tests rerun, GPU, RPC, full suite or product edits

reviewed_contracts.independent_locks: RGB/depth acquire only their own lock; wire acquires/releases each sequentially; RGB does not enter the depth lock even when cached
reviewed_contracts.at_most_once_success: Each encoded key is the successful-publication sentinel, inspected under component lock; raw buffer released only after its encoded value is stored
reviewed_contracts.retry: Component failure propagates native exception and retains own raw buffer; prior successful other component is preserved
reviewed_contracts.wire: Both components materialized; explicit reconstruction preserves metadata insertion order then RGB then depth across every access order
reviewed_contracts.bytes: JPEG RGB-to-BGR conversion quality90 and zlib depth level3 unchanged; nonfinite depth sanitization remains identical on depth encoding; no-depth key remains null
reviewed_contracts.ownership: Existing capture copies unchanged; independent raw references release independently and are bounded by retained frame objects
reviewed_contracts.physical_safety: No physics reads, camera cadence, capture anchors, history, timestamps, provenance, actuator paths, observer or depth consumers changed

new.provenance: Observed tool result retained explicitly; no invented raw log.

limits: No measured speedup or native acceptance follows from CPU tests. Controlled comparison and source-bound full validation remain parent work.
The 16 focused successes have observed tool-result provenance rather than a separately retained shell stdout log, accurately disclosed by author.
